name: SSD
provider: UNC Chapel Hill / Google / Zoox / University of Michigan

name: ELECTRA
aliases: Efficiently Learning an Encoder that Classifies Token Replacements Accurately

name: Random Forest
yearAnnotation: Breiman published Random Forests in the October 2001 issue of Machine Learning; the publisher establishes the month and year, not a release day.

name: Decision Tree
provider: Leo Breiman, Jerome Friedman, Richard Olshen, Charles Stone
yearAnnotation: The date and authors refer to the CART classification and regression method documented in the 1984 book Classification and Regression Trees, which is the basis of scikit-learn's tree implementation; decision trees as a broader family predate CART.

name: Support Vector Machine
yearAnnotation: Cortes and Vapnik published the soft-margin support-vector network in September 1995 while both were affiliated with AT&T Bell Laboratories in the United States; earlier support-vector formulations predate this paper.

name: K-Nearest Neighbors
yearAnnotation: Fix and Hodges issued their nearest-neighbor discrimination report in February 1951 at the University of California, Berkeley; the report is the historical milestone used here, not the introduction of every modern k-NN variant.

name: Naive Bayes
yearAnnotation: Bayes's 1763 essay is a foundation of Bayesian probability, not a release of the Naive Bayes classifier family; Maron's 1961 Automatic Indexing paper is an early classification application, but a unique inventor, country and release date are not established for the whole family.

name: XGBoost
yearAnnotation: The project's own release history dates its initial v0.1 release to March 26, 2014; the 2016 research paper and later package releases are not its initial release.

name: AdaBoost
yearAnnotation: Freund and Schapire introduced AdaBoost in their EuroCOLT 1995 paper; the 1996 experiments paper and the expanded 1997 journal article followed that introduction.

name: Gradient Boosting
yearAnnotation: The date records the October 2001 journal publication of Friedman's Greedy Function Approximation: A Gradient Boosting Machine; the paper originated as a 1999 lecture and manuscript, so 2001 is a publication milestone rather than the first conception of gradient boosting.

name: Autoencoder
provider: David Rumelhart, Geoffrey Hinton, Ronald Williams

name: Diffusion Model
provider: Jascha Sohl-Dickstein, Eric Weiss, Niru Maheswaranathan, Surya Ganguli

name: LightGBM
yearAnnotation: Microsoft Research dates the LightGBM project to October 2016; its NeurIPS paper appeared in 2017, and a 2017 tagged release is not the project's origin.

name: CatBoost
yearAnnotation: Yandex publicly announced and open-sourced the CatBoost library on July 18, 2017; the June 28 research preprint and subsequent GitHub tags describe different milestones.

name: Gaussian Process
yearAnnotation: Gaussian processes have a long history spanning time-series prediction, spatial kriging and machine learning; Krige's 1951 work on spatial prediction does not establish a unique inventor, country or release date for the Gaussian-process family.

name: Ridge Regression
yearAnnotation: Hoerl and Kennard published Ridge Regression: Biased Estimation for Nonorthogonal Problems in February 1970; this dates their statistical ridge formulation, not all earlier regularization methods.

aliases: Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator
name: Lasso
yearAnnotation: Tibshirani published Regression Shrinkage and Selection via the Lasso in 1996 while affiliated with the University of Toronto, Canada.

name: Elastic Net
yearAnnotation: Zou and Hastie introduced the elastic net in their 2005 paper Regularization and Variable Selection via the Elastic Net while affiliated with Stanford University in the United States.

name: Boltzmann Machine
provider: David Ackley, Geoffrey Hinton, Terrence Sejnowski

name: Linear Regression
yearAnnotation: Legendre published the method of least squares in Paris in 1805; this is a historical foundation for fitting linear regression, not a release of a modern software estimator.

name: Logistic Regression
yearAnnotation: Cox published The Regression Analysis of Binary Sequences in 1958; this is a foundational binary-regression formulation, while modern logistic regression also supports multiclass classification.

name: K-Means
yearAnnotation: The date records Lloyd's 1957 Bell Laboratories manuscript underlying the standard iterative algorithm; his paper was formally published in 1982, and the name k-means and other formulations have separate histories.

aliases: Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise
name: DBSCAN
provider: Martin Ester, Hans-Peter Kriegel, Jörg Sander, Xiaowei Xu
yearAnnotation: Ester, Kriegel, Sander and Xu introduced DBSCAN in the KDD 1996 proceedings published by AAAI; all four authors were affiliated with the University of Munich, Germany.

name: PCA
yearAnnotation: Pearson published On Lines and Planes of Closest Fit to Systems of Points in Space in November 1901; the year records that publication, not later PCA implementations.

name: Gaussian Mixture Model
yearAnnotation: Pearson studied fitting mixtures of normal distributions in his 1894 Contributions to the Mathematical Theory of Evolution; only the year is recorded here, without an invented January 1 release day.

name: Perceptron
yearAnnotation: Rosenblatt described the perceptron in his January 1957 Cornell Aeronautical Laboratory report; the 1958 journal paper and later hardware demonstrations are separate milestones.

name: Multi-Layer Perceptron
yearAnnotation: Rosenblatt documented multilayer perceptron architectures in Principles of Neurodynamics in 1962; Rumelhart, Hinton and Williams described influential backpropagation training in 1986, but neither date establishes a unique release of the generic architecture.

name: Linear Discriminant Analysis
yearAnnotation: Fisher published The Use of Multiple Measurements in Taxonomic Problems in 1936, a foundational linear discriminant formulation.

name: Isolation Forest
provider: Fei Tony Liu, Kai Ming Ting, Zhi-Hua Zhou
yearAnnotation: Liu, Ting and Zhou introduced Isolation Forest in the ICDM 2008 proceedings with affiliations at Monash University, Australia, and Nanjing University, China; the conference ran December 15-19, which does not establish the paper's release day.

name: Agglomerative Clustering
yearAnnotation: The date records Sokal and Michener's 1958 publication of a numerical-taxonomy method using average-linkage clustering; agglomerative clustering comprises multiple linkage methods and has no single release date for the whole family.

name: Spectral Clustering
provider: Andrew Ng, Michael Jordan, Yair Weiss
yearAnnotation: The date records Ng, Jordan and Weiss's NIPS 2001 spectral-clustering paper, with affiliations in the United States; spectral graph methods and normalized cuts predate this particular algorithm.

name: Mean Shift
yearAnnotation: Fukunaga and Hostetler published the mean-shift density-gradient procedure in January 1975; the work was carried out at Purdue University in the United States.

name: Affinity Propagation
yearAnnotation: Frey and Dueck's Clustering by Passing Messages Between Data Points was published online on January 11, 2007, before the February 16 Science print issue.

aliases: Ordering Points To Identify the Clustering Structure
name: OPTICS
provider: Mihael Ankerst, Markus Breunig, Hans-Peter Kriegel, Jörg Sander
yearAnnotation: Ankerst, Breunig, Kriegel and Sander introduced OPTICS in the SIGMOD 1999 proceedings; the conference start does not independently establish a first-publication day.

name: Kernel PCA
provider: Bernhard Schölkopf, Alexander Smola, and Klaus-Robert Müller
yearAnnotation: Schölkopf, Smola and Müller described kernel PCA in the 1996 Max Planck technical report Nonlinear Component Analysis as a Kernel Eigenvalue Problem; the ICANN 1997 paper and 1998 journal article followed it.

name: Independent Component Analysis
yearAnnotation: The date records Comon's 1994 paper Independent Component Analysis, A New Concept? from Thomson-Sintra in France; Hyvärinen and Oja's later FastICA work is a separate algorithmic contribution.

name: Non-negative Matrix Factorization
yearAnnotation: The date records Lee and Seung's October 21, 1999 Nature paper on learning parts-based representations; earlier non-negative factorization work, including Paatero and Tapper's 1994 positive matrix factorization, predates this milestone.

name: Truncated SVD
yearAnnotation: Eckart and Young published the low-rank matrix approximation result underlying truncated SVD in September 1936; this dates the approximation theorem, not the invention of the full SVD or a particular software implementation.

name: t-SNE
provider: Laurens van der Maaten, Geoffrey Hinton
yearAnnotation: Van der Maaten and Hinton introduced t-SNE in November 2008 with affiliations at Tilburg University, Netherlands, and the University of Toronto, Canada.

name: Quadratic Discriminant Analysis
yearAnnotation: The year follows the 1947 offprint of Smith's Some Examples of Discrimination catalogued in his UCL papers; Wiley's digital record labels the volume January 1946, so the archival offprint is used rather than silently treating the conflicting metadata as an exact date.

name: Local Outlier Factor
provider: Markus Breunig, Hans-Peter Kriegel, Raymond Ng, and Jörg Sander
yearAnnotation: Breunig, Kriegel, Ng and Sander introduced LOF in the SIGMOD 2000 proceedings with affiliations in Germany and Canada; the conference start is not used as a first-publication day.

name: One-Class SVM
provider: Bernhard Schölkopf, John Platt, John Shawe-Taylor, Alex Smola, and Robert Williamson
yearAnnotation: Schölkopf, Williamson, Smola, Shawe-Taylor and Platt introduced this unlabeled-data novelty-detection method at NIPS 1999 with affiliations in the United Kingdom, Australia and the United States.

name: Hidden Markov Model
yearAnnotation: Baum and Petrie published Statistical Inference for Probabilistic Functions of Finite State Markov Chains in December 1966, a foundational HMM inference paper; modern Python HMM implementations are maintained in hmmlearn rather than scikit-learn.

name: Conditional Random Field
provider: John Lafferty, Andrew McCallum, Fernando Pereira
yearAnnotation: Lafferty, McCallum and Pereira introduced Conditional Random Fields in their ICML 2001 paper; sklearn-crfsuite provides a scikit-learn-compatible estimator, but CRFs are not implemented in scikit-learn itself.

name: SURF
provider: Herbert Bay, Tinne Tuytelaars and Luc Van Gool

name: ORB
provider: Ethan Rublee, Vincent Rabaud, Kurt Konolige and Gary Bradski

name: BRIEF
provider: Michael Calonder, Vincent Lepetit, Christoph Strecha and Pascal Fua

name: Local Binary Pattern
provider: Timo Ojala, Matti Pietikäinen and David Harwood

name: GrabCut
provider: Carsten Rother, Vladimir Kolmogorov and Andrew Blake
